articles.author: hello@smashingmagazine.com (Godstime Aburu)
articles.description: Dropdowns often work perfectly until they’re placed inside a scrollable panel, where they can get clipped, and half the menu disappears behind the container’s edge. Godstime Aburu explains why this happens and offers practical solutions to fix it.
articles.title: Dropdowns Inside Scrollable Containers: Why They Break And How To Fix Them Properly

articles.author: hello@smashingmagazine.com (Vitaly Friedman)
articles.description: How to choose between modals and pages, when to avoid modals, and how to determine the right level of interruption or navigation. Brought to you by Smart Interface Design Patterns, a **friendly video course on UX** and design patterns by Vitaly.
articles.title: Modal vs. Separate Page: UX Decision Tree

articles.author: hello@smashingmagazine.com (Alan Cohen)
articles.description: Design is about pacing and feelings as much as pixels and patterns. Alan Cohen explores Emotion in Flow and Emotion in Conflict, showing how anime like Dan Da Dan and superhero films like James Gunn’s Superman manage emotional shifts and translating those ideas into practical patterns for product design.
articles.title: Anime vs. Marvel/DC: Designing Digital Products With Emotion In Flow

articles.author: hello@smashingmagazine.com (Joe Attardi)
articles.description: The way JavaScript handles time has evolved significantly, from the built-in `Date` API to Moment.js and now Temporal. The new standard fills gaps in the original `Date` API while addressing limitations found in Moment and other libraries. Joe Attardi shares practical “recipes” for migrating Moment-based code to the new Temporal API.
articles.title: Moving From Moment.js To The JS Temporal API

articles.author: hello@smashingmagazine.com (Brecht De Ruyte)
articles.description: For years, developers have been hacking around the limitations of `border-radius`, using clip-path, SVG masks, and fragile workarounds just to get anything other than round corners. The new `corner-shape` property finally changes that, opening the door to beveled, scooped, and squircle corners.
articles.title: Beyond `border-radius`: What The CSS `corner-shape` Property Unlocks For Everyday UI

articles.author: hello@smashingmagazine.com (Sunil Sandhu)
articles.description: Some forms stay UI, while others quietly become rule engines. Here’s why these two different approaches exist and how to choose between them.
articles.title: Building Dynamic Forms In React And Next.js

articles.author: hello@smashingmagazine.com (Anders Toxboe)
articles.description: Many product teams still lean on usability improvements and isolated behavioral tweaks to address weak activation, drop-offs, and low retention – only to see results plateau or slip into shallow gamification. Anders Toxboe updates persuasive design for today’s reality, clarifying what has actually held up over the last decade.
articles.title: Persuasive Design: Ten Years Later

articles.author: hello@smashingmagazine.com (Carrie Webster)
articles.description: UX design is entering a new phase, with designers shifting from makers of outputs to directors of intent. AI can now generate wireframes, prototypes, and even design systems in minutes, but UX has never been only about creating interfaces. It’s about navigating ambiguity, advocating for humans in systems optimised for efficiency, and solving their problems through thoughtful design.
articles.title: Human Strategy In An AI-Accelerated Workflow

articles.author: hello@smashingmagazine.com (Ari Stiles)
articles.description: Our newest Smashing Book, “Accessible UX Research” by Michele Williams, is finally shipping worldwide — and we couldn’t be happier! This book is about research, but you’ll also learn about assistive technology, different types of disability, and how to build accessibility into the entire design process. This thoughtful book will get you thinking about ways to make your UX research more inclusive and thorough, no matter your budget or timeline. Jump to the book details or order your copy now.
articles.title: Now Shipping: Accessible UX Research, A New Smashing Book By Michele Williams

articles.author: hello@smashingmagazine.com (Godstime Aburu)
articles.description: What happens if you rebuild a single tooltip using the browser’s native model without the aid of a library? The Popover API turns tooltips from something you simulate into something the browser actually understands. Opening and closing, keyboard interaction, Escape handling, and much of the accessibility now come from the platform itself, not from ad-hoc JavaScript.
articles.title: Getting Started With The Popover API

articles.author: hello@smashingmagazine.com (Cosima Mielke)
articles.description: Do you need a little inspiration boost? Well, then our new batch of desktop wallpapers is for you. Designed by the community for the community, the wallpapers in this collection are the perfect opportunity to get your desktop ready for spring — and, who knows, maybe they’ll spark some new ideas, too. Enjoy!
articles.title: Fresh Energy In March (2026 Wallpapers Edition)

articles.author: hello@smashingmagazine.com (Iris Lješnjanin)
articles.description: Meet our brand new conference for designers and UI engineers who love the web. That’s [SmashingConf Amsterdam](https://smashingconf.com/amsterdam-2026), taking place in the legendary Pathé Tuschinski, on April 13–16, 2026.
articles.title: Say Cheese! Meet SmashingConf Amsterdam 🇳🇱

articles.author: hello@smashingmagazine.com (Carrie Webster)
articles.description: Every high-resolution hero image, autoplay video, and complex JavaScript animation carries a cost. Sustainable UX challenges the era of “unlimited pixels” and reframes performance as responsibility. In 2026, truly sophisticated design is defined not by how much it adds, but by how thoughtfully it reduces its footprint.
articles.title: A Designer’s Guide To Eco-Friendly Interfaces
